mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as reduced borrowing costs stimulate corporate investment and equity valuations.
evidence_refs: fact:Current FEDFUNDS at 2.5% is below historical average of 5.5% (2000-2005)
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 3%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.3 percentage points over three months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:UNRATE at 5.4% in Feb 2005, up from 5.1% in Nov 2004 (3-month change: +0.3pp)
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances (UNRATE rise > 0.3pp in 3 months), or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) from the prior month indicate weakening consumer demand, reducing corporate revenue expectations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline from prior month
evidence_refs: fact:HOUST at 2144.0 (Jan 2005, down from 2159.0 in Dec 2004) and RSAFS at 325308.0 (Feb 2005, down from 352138.0 in Jan 2005)
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline from prior month, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply shock regime (defined by industrial production (INDPRO) declining below its 12-month moving average), reduced manufacturing output and potential input cost pressures lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:INDPRO at 95.88 (Jan 2005, down from 117.667 in Dec 2004)
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is below its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 2.5% signals persistent inflation, prompting aggressive monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY change exceeds 2.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) supports stronger labor market conditions, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:PAYEMS at 133034.0 (Feb 2005, up from 132843.0 in Jan 2005)
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS is above its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a growth slowdown regime (defined by annualized real GDP growth (GDPC1) below 1.5%), reduced economic expansion leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to lower corporate investment and consumer confidence.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 annualized growth is below 1.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and high year-over-year inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises from prior month and CPIAUCSL YoY change > 2.5%
evidence_refs: fact:FEDFUNDS stable at 2.5% (Feb 2005) and CPIAUCSL YoY change at 2.7% (Jan 2005)
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.
